maya: Evening check — scheduled change window tonight 22:00 UTC. This deploy touches API header split, runtime kernel tweak (kv eviction TTL default), and console schema v2. We need a quick agreement on pinned versions and rollback gates.

liam: I have a runtime build that switches kernel A->B for batching perf. Can we pin runtime to v3.4.1 for canary? Kernel B has slightly different KV eviction behavior (longer TTL). If we don't pin, downstream console may misread route metadata.

sophia: Console schema v2 adds route_metadata.health_tags. If runtime TTL changes, some health checks will flake. We can make console tolerate missing tags for 5m but prefer pinning to avoid alerts.

noah: Router header-split requires a 5min ramp and sticky session toggle. If API isn't in sync, we'll end up with 4xx for clients relying on old header. Recommend: API pinned to 2.11.0-canary -> router rule staged -> runtime pinned -> gradual traffic shift.

deploy-bot: preflight checks started for 1743022222

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: lint OK

deploy-bot: :warning: canary smoke tests failing for api@2.11.0-canary in eu-west-1 (timeout on /v1/health) — investigating

maya: noted. liam, can runtime canary run with the api@2.11.0-canary? If api health endpoint is flaky we'll need a fallback plan.

liam: runtime v3.4.1 can run with api@2.11.0-canary, but kernel B has a different seq-length path which increases p50 by ~10ms. That's acceptable. I'll annotate the rollback step: revert runtime to v3.3.9 and restore kernel A.

sophia: Add console fallback: if route_metadata.health_tags missing, treat as legacy and use a conservative TTL of 30s. I'll put that behind feature-flag cf-console-legacy-health for the window.

noah: Router plan: start with 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 15m. If error rate >1% or latency p95 regresses >200ms during any step, abort and rollback router rules.

maya: Rollback criteria summary (draft):
- api: if /v1/health fails >3 consecutive checks during canary, revert to api@2.10.4
- runtime: if p95 tokens latency or error rate spikes beyond baseline + 3σ, revert to v3.3.9
- router: abort on >1% 5xx or p95 +200ms; revert sticky and header-split
- console: if consumer-facing dashboards show >5% missing metadata, toggle cf-console-legacy-health off and rollback schema v2

julia: I'll update release notes and capture exact commit hashes. Also opening a short runbook: https://internal.redwood/rel/1743022222 (add manual rollback commands)

maya: quick ops commands in runbook (for visibility):
```
# revert api
kubectl -n api set image deploy/api api=redwood/api:2.10.4
# revert runtime
kubectl -n runtime set image daemon/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:v3.3.9
# rollback router rules
curl -X POST https://orch/reverts/router -d '{"release": "1743022222"}'
```

liam: I'll keep an eye on kv eviction metrics and heap churn during canary. ping me @liam if smoke test flaps.

sophia: I'll attach the console feature-flag toggle to the deploy-bot flow so it can be turned off fast.

deploy-bot: preflight checks re-run: :white_check_mark: smoke passed for api@2.11.0-canary in us-east-1, :white_check_mark: runtime smoke OK, :white_check_mark: console FF toggles available

maya: Final sign-off? I need two approvals to proceed into the window.

noah: +1 from router side

liam: +1 runtime

sophia: +1 console

julia: +1 release docs and runbook

maya: Great — proceeding to staged rollout at 22:00 UTC. I'll paste the release-note blurb once it's live.

julia: Release note: "Cross-service header-split and runtime kernel upgrade — pinned variants for safe rollout. Change window 22:00 UTC. See runbook https://internal.redwood/rel/1743022222"

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
